subject: Follow-up: capture decision map, SOC/compliance owners, and econ buyer
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@meditech.com>, Tom Harris <tom.harris@meditech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 8 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: capture decision map, SOC/compliance owners, and econ buyer

Thanks again for taking the time today — great call. Quick recap and the items we agreed to capture so Redwoods' side can start the intake and security/eval process:

- Goal: scope a 3-month pilot of Redwood Dedicated for clinical-document summarization (low-latency inference near EHR systems).
- Success criteria (customer-provided): latency under 350ms p95 for 512-token sequences, redaction of PHI, and <2% accuracy regression vs. baseline QA prompts.
- Next immediate asks from our side: org/decision map (who signs for procurement, who owns security/compliance evidence), designated econ buyer, and any standard legal terms or procurement steps we should expect.

Could you please:
1) Share a high-level org chart or list of stakeholders (names + roles + emails) who will be involved in procurement, security/compliance review, and pilot sign-off.
2) Confirm who the economic buyer is for this engagement and their preferred cadence for decisioning (e.g., single approval vs. committee).
3) Point us to the SOC2/PII evidence contact and any specific data residency or logging constraints we should be aware of.

If easier, a one-page PDF or spreadsheet with the columns: name | role | area (procurement/security/clinical) | email would be perfect. Happy to take that and stitch together a mutual action plan and proposed timelines.

Proposed next step: If you can share the roster by next Tue (2027-04-12), we’ll propose a short alignment call the following week to review the security checklist and slot a technical review.

Thanks again — I’ll pull together a draft MAP (mutual action plan) once we have the roster.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: (internal meeting notes referenced)
From: Alicia Nguyen <alicia@meditech.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom.harris@meditech.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: capture decision map, SOC/compliance owners, and econ buyer

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the recap and clear asks. Attaching a cleaned-up org chart and a short SOC2 summary that our InfoSec manager put together. A few notes inline:

- Econ buyer: Tom Harris (Director of Digital Modernization) — he’ll own budget approval and final pilot sign-off.
- Procurement lead: Linda Park (contracts@meditech.com) — she handles the POs and master services agreement redlines. I don’t want to add her to all threads yet but copying her contact card in the attachments.
- InfoSec/Security evidence owner: Rajiv Patel, InfoSec Manager (rajiv.patel@meditech.com) — he will coordinate SOC2 evidence, pen-test artifacts, and the security questionnaire.

I’ve attached: meditech-org-chart-v2.pdf (high level), SOC2-summary.xlsx (controls matrix excerpt), procurement-contact-card.vcf (Linda Park).

For our timeline: Tom wants a short economic overview and SLA summary by the 3rd week of April. Rajiv has requested our security checklist to kick off the evidence exchange — can your security lead share the standard SOC2 artifact list and an engineer who can do the technical deep-dive?

I can be the day-to-day contact — happy to coordinate time for the technical review.

Best,
Alicia Nguyen
Head of Partnerships, Meditech Systems
Alicia.Nguyen@meditech.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: capture decision map, SOC/compliance owners, and econ buyer

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Alicia — the attachments help a lot. A couple quick clarifying questions so we can scope the security kickoff properly:

1) Rajiv — will you want us to submit a full security questionnaire first (example: CAIQ + our Redwood security pack) or start with the SOC2 artifact exchange? We’ll prepare both but want to align on the preferred intake to minimize duplicate work.
2) Are there any specific data isolation or logging retention requirements for the pilot (region-specific EHR hosting, data-at-rest encryption keys, or minimum audit log retention)? If those exist, please flag them so we can align our Dedicated deployment profile and KMS configuration.

Proposed attendees for the technical review: Ben Carter (Redwood infra lead, security intake), Marissa Cole (solution architect) — Vanessa will coordinate times. We expect a 60-minute technical review + a 30-minute procurement intro if useful.

If Linda (procurement) prefers, we can send a short procurement checklist and standard commercial terms in advance to speed up the PO process.

Thanks — ping us any preferred times next week and we’ll send a calendar invite.

—
Ben Carter
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com
